summary: Louis Dumont was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Marcel Mauss, Walther Schubring, and Alain Froment at institutions including the Institut d'ethnologie and EPHE, later holding posts at Oxford, EPHE, and EHESS.

Louis Finot worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École des chartes and under Sylvain Lévi, later serving as director of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient and professor honoraire at the Collège de France.
Louis Gabaude is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who held a post at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient around 1980.

Louis H. Gray specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Princeton and earned his Ph.D. at Columbia, later holding posts at Princeton and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

Louis Havet was a linguistics scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne. From 1885 to 1925, he served as professor and Latin philology chair at the Collège de France.

Louis Renou was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch at EPHE and other Paris institutions. He taught at the University of Lyon, Sorbonne, EPHE, and directed the Institut de civilisation indienne.

Louis de La Vallée Poussin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Liège, KU Leuven, the Sorbonne, and Leiden under mentors including Sylvain Lévi, and served as professor at Ghent University from 1893 to 1929.

Louis-Mathieu Langlès was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar who studied at the Collège de France under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served as chief keeper at the Bibliothèque nationale and administrator at INALCO, which he founded in 1795.

Louise Allison Cort is a specialist in Japanology and history/archaeology. She studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College, and served as ceramics curator at the Freer and Sackler Galleries of the Smithsonian Institution from circa 1981 to 2020.

Louise Child is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, also studying under Ringu Tulku, and held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at Gauhati University, attested in 1999 under supervisor Sibnath Sarma, and also studied under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Lourens P. van den Bosch is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Groningen and earned his PhD under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University. He also held an assistantship at the University of Groningen.
Lozang Samten studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Trijang Rinpoche.
Luboš Bělka is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from 1978 to 1983 and later held a post there around 1993.

Luca Maria Olivieri is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who received his doctorate from the Free University of Berlin. He directed the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and held a professorship at Ca' Foscari University.

Lucia Dolce is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies who has held posts as lecturer and associate professor in Japanese religions at SOAS University of London, attested between 2003 and 2015.
Lucia Galli is a Tibetology scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held a post there.

Lucian Scherman was an Indologist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau and completed his doctorate and habilitation under Ernst Kuhn at the University of Munich, where he served as professor and led the Museum Fünf Kontinente.

Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He taught Italian at the University of Allahabad and served as Chair of History of Eastern Asia at the University of Rome from 1955 to 1984.
